Distinct legal structured layout leaves are silently coalesced in CC/R envelopes. layout_leaves inserts both interface_regions["a"]["c.db"] and interface_regions["a.c"]["db"] under the same BTreeMap key "interface_regions.a.c.db"; the latter overwrites the former. Round 11 correctly selects each oracle by its exact owner before flattening, but CC/R must retain both owners and still lose the first leaf. sol.fix:
Change reference-interpreter/src/identity.rs::layout_leaves and Object::envelope to retain a lossless collection of structured leaves, including original key components, through selection and serialization. Do not key the collection solely by the non-injective dotted rendering. Preserve the round-11 exact-owner oracle selection; emit every selected leaf once, including both colliding rendered paths for CC/R. Adapt lproc global lookup/image collection to the lossless representation without changing their closure selection.
Determining specification: §9.2 says "CC / R function: all `layout` leaves, every data image they name"; part (5b) says "for every layout leaf in the closure set, sorted by dotted path bytewise". It identifies "interface_regions.<oracle>.<region>" as leaves; §16.1 NAME permits dots. Neither dropping a leaf nor rejecting these names implements those sentences.
There is a genuine tie-order gap: stable structured-key traversal and sorting equal-path lines by their JCS values are both defensible because §9.2 specifies no ordering within a dotted-path tie. Neither reading permits overwriting. Choose stable bytewise original-component order as the tie breaker: it preserves structural ownership and is independent of the values being hashed. Add a SPEC-QUESTIONS entry with this proposed wording: "Emit one line for every structured layout leaf, including leaves with coincident dotted renderings. Sort by the rendered dotted path bytewise; break ties bytewise by the sequence of original JSON key components." No accepted-spec edit or ban on dotted names is needed for this review fix.
Add tests/identity.rs::r12_cc_r_layout_paths_preserve_colliding_leaves and tests/cli_xam.rs::r12_cli_checks_lossless_layout_envelopes. Use the literal object above (or extend r11_case("deep-a-32") without support::rehash), with this exact main envelope, final LF included:

ptr_width=32

fn cc @main () () () () ()
^entry():
ret

layout heap_base 128
layout heap_limit_max 0
layout interface_regions.a.c.db {"base":16}
layout interface_regions.a.c.db {"base":32}

Repeat with fn r and signature kind/tier r: expected main hashes are 68943b7ebec4b123a9b0aed04af75e1e037545794a3dee8a3aaceb7b623d421a at 16 and 54af133bf40f7db2ca5da434db35f34f2157ae1808b46ed80137481e4a9efc17 at 17. codex.fix: Change src/identity.rs::layout_leaves and Object::envelope to preserve each structural leaf, for example a sequence carrying original key components, rendered path and value. Apply closure selection using structural keys, then sort and serialize every selected leaf, retaining duplicates in the rendered path. Update layout_leaves consumers as needed so a dotted string is never used as unique structural identity. Do not ban legal dots. The determining §9.2 text is '(5b) for every layout leaf in the closure set, sorted by dotted path bytewise' and 'CC / R function: all layout leaves, every data image they name'. §16.1 allows dots in NAME. Expected: the two identical layout interface_regions.a.b.c lines in the literal envelope above, both expected interface/closure hashes, and successful check for both supplied variants. Add tests/identity.rs::r12_cc_r_colliding_dotted_leaves: parse each literal object, assert exact envelope bytes, assert its expected interface AND closure hashes, and call check_hashes successfully; add a CLI check/hash counterpart in tests/cli_xam.rs. These assertions fail on this snapshot and should pass after the fix. Retain the round-11 exact-owner oracle tests; changing a foreign owner's base must still not change an oracle's envelope. For unequal-valued leaves at equal rendered paths, the spec lacks a secondary order. Sorting tied entries by original structured keys or by rendered value are both possible refinements; choose structured keys because they retain schema ownership and give a stable value-independent order. Add a SPEC-QUESTIONS entry and propose this §9.2 wording: 'Retain one entry for every structural layout leaf. Sort by rendered dotted path bytewise; ties are ordered by the sequence of original JSON member keys, compared component-wise bytewise.' Then add own-leaf sensitivity tests for each colliding leaf. This tie-order clarification does not affect the equal-value failing witness.

codex.problem:
Object::validate_symbols rejects every oracle interface-region name that also occurs in symbols or imports, even when the symbol is a function and cannot denote a global address. The comment asserts that §9.2 requires this ban, but §4.2 resolves lift.addr through globals or the current oracle's interface and §9.2 explicitly leaves interface-region references unchanged. No SPEC-QUESTIONS entry records this scope reduction. The following independently pinned, LF-terminated oracle has a local region o, no globals and no ambiguity: lift.addr @o can only name its interface region, not its own function definition.
